messages:
incident-bot: PAGER DUTY ALERT (P1): High error rate on private VPN for customer acme-corp (privateconnect-123). Symptoms: intermittent packet loss and app sessions dropping. Triggers: 5xx proxy errors + BGP withdraws. https://redwood.ops/incidents/1803005678

oncall-eli: taking this. paging emergency oncall now. prepping timeline — what's the customer impact?

maria: customer says their internal APIs to 10.10.2.0/24 are failing from on-prem in short bursts (~1-2s) across multiple hosts, not a single flow.

sachin: seeing BGP flap on our transit gateway toward their VGW. Timestamps match the VPN tunnel renegotiation windows. Suspect IPsec SA rekey drift between tunnels.

netops-bot: Observed events: [AWS] VPN vpn-0a1b2c3d: tunnel1 (us-east-2a) rekey 18:03:21Z, tunnel2 (us-east-2b) rekey 18:03:22Z, multiple SA resets within 30s.

oncall-eli: confirm both tunnels are up but flapping on rekey. Any infra-level packet drops (EC2 NATs/VPCs)?

jordan: ENIs look healthy. Flow logs show SYN+ACK returned then TCP RST within 1-2s. Traces show next-hop differences during the same 2s window. Example: 
```
traceroute to 10.10.2.15 (10.10.2.15), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.63 ms  0.49 ms  0.45 ms
 2  100.64.0.5  4.32 ms  4.27 ms  4.21 ms
 3  10.200.1.1  18.11 ms  *  18.03 ms
```
Alternate run shows different next-hop in same window.

maria: customer pasted their edge debug: 
```
# show crypto ipsec sa
interface: Tunnel0
   local 1.2.3.4 remote 5.6.7.8
   active SAs: 2, origin: crypto map
   in use settings=esm tunnel, dpd=enabled
   # pkts encaps: 12345, decaps: 12340, replay detection: enabled
   # last rekey: 00:00:58
```
They report SAs rekeying every ~60s, unusually frequent.

sachin: SA lifetime mismatch likely. If one side rekeys much earlier, you'll get overlapping SAs and traffic can be dropped during swaps. Our VPN profile default lifetime is 3600s. Why 60s?

aws-ops-contact: investigating vendor side. Customer edge had a firmware update earlier today; their appliance may be sending aggressive lifetimes. Opening vendor ticket.

customer-support: informed customer and gave a temporary mitigation plan; they asked for ETA and steps.

oncall-eli: mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic to tunnel2 (us-east-2b) while stabilizing tunnel1; 2) temporarily prefer tunnel2 via route update to avoid flaps; 3) ask customer to rollback firmware or align SA lifetime to 3600s.

sachin: implementing route preference now — updating route table to prefer T2. Runbook command: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd1234 --destination-cidr-block 10.10.2.0/24 --instance-id eni-0f1e2d3c
```
Applying.

netops-bot: Route update successful. Traffic now prefers tunnel2 (us-east-2b). Monitoring for 3 minutes.

(1m later)

jordan: metrics: 5xx error rate dropped from ~12% -> ~1.1% after route shift. TCP resets reduced. Residual failures for long-lived sessions mid-handshake.

maria: customer reports sessions mostly restored but still intermittent 1-2s blips ~every 10 minutes. Could be DPD or NAT session timers on their firewall.

oncall-eli: vendor suggests disabling aggressive rekey (esp lifetime 60s) or patching edge to stable. Sample command for their device: 
```
crypto ipsec security-association lifetime seconds 3600
crypto ipsec security-association lifetime kilobytes 0
```

aws-ops-contact: AWS side is clear; rekey events originate from peer.

customer-support: drafting impact summary for customer ops: "Intermittent connectivity to services in us-east-2a observed 18:03-18:15 UTC; ~15% of requests impacted during peak. Root cause: mismatched IPsec SA lifetimes on customer edge causing tunnel flips. Temporary mitigation: traffic routed to secondary tunnel in us-east-2b. Next steps: align SA lifetime or rollback edge firmware."

oncall-eli: assigning postmortem owner: @jordan. Severity remains P1 until stable for 1 hour.

sara: I'll take handoff in 45m. Add notes in the incident doc and escalate to infra if tunnel2 load >85%.

jordan: created incident doc + timeline + logs: https://redwood.ops/incidents/1803005678/postmortem. Postmortem owner assigned.

oncall-eli: notify customer success & legal re possible SLA hit; update customer with recommended config and ask for confirmation when applied.

customer-support: emailed recommended config and asked customer to confirm after testing in staging. Customer acknowledged.

netops-bot: Monitoring window 60m started. Will alert on packet loss or BGP withdraws.

(45m later)

sachin: no new aggressive rekeys observed from peer. Metrics stable: 0.2% 5xx over last 15m. Marking as mitigated but not closed.

oncall-eli: handing off to @sara for escalation if needed. I'll stay available for 15m then close pager. Good work team :thumbsup:

sara: acknowledged. I'll monitor until customer confirms patch/rollback. Will reopen if they hit issues during change.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigated -> Monitoring. P1 remains open until customer confirms permanent fix. Owner: jordan. Handoff: sara."
